flags: The company refinanced its senior notes and amended and restated its revolving credit facility, and booked a one-time loss on extinguishment of debt of $51.4 million.
The company settled its obligations under its defined benefit pension plan and recorded a one-time non-cash pension settlement charge of $33.8 million.
The company published a raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance range of $5.90 to $6.10, up from $5.15 to $5.45.
no_value_reason: minority interests take too large a share of income

business_model.claim: Tutor Perini sells construction services (general contracting, construction management and design-build) to private customers and public agencies.
quotes: is a leading construction company offering diversified general contracting, construction management and design-build services to private customers and public agencies throughout the world.

business_model.claim: The business reports three segments: Civil, Building and Specialty Contractors.
quotes: Our business is conducted through three segments: Civil, Building and Specialty Contractors.

business_model.basis: Segment description is stated in the 10-K. Backlog figures are from the earnings release backlog table.
business_model.claim: Civil does public-works and infrastructure construction and is the largest segment by backlog: $10,006.9 of $20,353.3 total (table in millions).
quotes: Our Civil segment specializes in public works construction and the replacement and reconstruction of infrastructure across several major geographic regions of the United States.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the release segment table.
business_model.claim: Building serves private and public building customers, with a stated leadership position in hospitality and gaming. Its revenue from external customers was $1,573,110 (table in thousands) for the latest nine months.
quotes: We are a recognized leader in the hospitality and gaming market, specializing in the construction of high-end resorts and casinos.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the release segment table.
business_model.claim: Specialty Contractors does electrical, mechanical, plumbing, HVAC and fire-protection work. Much of it is performed for the Civil and Building segments, and its revenue from external customers was $766,266 (table in thousands) for the latest nine months.
quotes: A significant portion of the segment's work has been, and is expected to continue to be, performed for our Civil and Building segments

business_model.basis: Taken directly from the segment information table; the attribution of share-based compensation to Corporate is inferred.
business_model.claim: For the latest nine months, Civil produced most of the segment operating income: $337,493, against $74,781 for Building and $16,398 for Specialty Contractors. Unallocated corporate costs were $(126,336) (table in thousands).
Customers are mostly government entities, which accounted for 86% of backlog at the last year-end.
quotes: The percentage of our business coming from government entities has continued to increase in recent years, and as of December 31, 2025 accounted for 86% of our backlog.

business_model.claim: Civil demand depends on public funding sources such as loans and grants, tax revenue and bonds, and for certain projects private capital.
quotes: Funding for major Civil segment infrastructure projects is typically provided through a combination of one or more of the following: local, regional, state and federal loans and grants; other direct allocations sourced through tax revenue; bonds; user fees; and, for certain projects, private capital.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; figures are from the income statement.
business_model.claim: Revenue growth comes mainly from executing newer, larger projects. Revenue was $4,746,761 for the latest nine months against $4,035,674 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: primarily driven by increased project execution activities on certain newer, larger and higher-margin projects that have significant scope of work remaining.

business_model.basis: Conversion timing is stated in the 10-K; the awards and backlog figures are from the release table.
business_model.claim: Backlog converts to revenue over several years, and new awards must replace the revenue recognized. Over the latest nine months, new awards of $4,540.3 were below revenue recognized of $(4,746.8), and backlog moved from $20,559.8 to $20,353.3 (table in millions).
quotes: Most projects in the Civil segment’s backlog typically convert to revenue over a period of three to five years and in the Building and Specialty Contractors segments over a period of one to three years.

business_model.basis: Figures are from the income statement; the breakdown of cost components is inferred and not itemized in the evidence.
business_model.claim: Cost of operations is the main cost line. In the latest nine months it was 4,159,388 against revenue of 4,746,761, leaving gross profit of 587,373, with general and administrative expense of 285,037 (table in thousands).
Vertical integration lets the company self-perform more of the work than competitors, which it presents as a bidding and execution advantage.
quotes: Our vertical integration capabilities, which also involve close interactions between our Civil and Building segment resources on large, complex projects, are a competitive advantage that allow us to self-perform a greater amount of work than our competitors.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Project margins depend on cost estimates and inflation or tariff exposure. The company says it mitigates this by transferring escalation risk to vendors and subcontractors.
quotes: If we are unable to accurately estimate contract risks, revenue or costs, we may incur a loss or achieve lower than anticipated profit.
Also at that time, the Company enters into fixed-price contracts with its key project subcontractors whereby the risk of unforeseen escalation is transferred to the subcontractors.

business_model.basis: Mechanism is stated in the 10-K; amounts are from the cash flow statement.
business_model.claim: Share-based compensation is a swing cost tied to the stock price. It was 77,179 for the latest nine months against 120,676 a year earlier (table in thousands).
quotes: These liability-classified awards are remeasured at fair value at the end of each reporting period with the change recognized in earnings.

business_model.basis: Balance sheet and cash flow figures are stated; the funding interpretation is inferred.
business_model.claim: Customer billings in advance fund much of the working capital. Billings in excess of costs and estimated earnings were 2,044,207, well above costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings of 767,432 (table in thousands). Operating cash flow was 665,063 for the nine months.

business_model.basis: Risk is stated in the 10-K; the balance trend is stated in the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Extra work and disputes can slow cash conversion and cut profit. The company reports a lower balance of unbilled costs: costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings were $767.4 million, which the release calls the lowest balance since the end of 2014.
quotes: Our contracts often require us to perform extra work beyond the initial project scope, which can result in disputes or claims and adversely affect our working capital, profits and cash flows.

business_model.basis: The risk is stated in the 10-K; the income figures are from the income statement. That the noncontrolling interests relate to joint ventures is inferred.
business_model.claim: Joint ventures are part of how projects are won, and partners' share of earnings reduces profit attributable to shareholders. Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was 49,336 of net income of 161,475 for the nine months (table in thousands).
quotes: Generally, we and our joint venture partners are jointly and severally liable for all liabilities and obligations of our joint ventures.

business_model.claim: Surety bonding capacity is a condition for winning work, because contracts often require performance bonds.
quotes: We are often required to provide surety bonds securing our performance under our contracts.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K business section; the advantage itself is management's assertion.
competitive_position.claim: The company says its vertical integration, which lets it self-perform more work than competitors, is a competitive advantage on large, complex projects.
quotes: Our vertical integration capabilities, which also involve close interactions between our Civil and Building segment resources on large, complex projects, are a competitive advantage that allow us to self-perform a greater amount of work than our competitors.

competitive_position.claim: Financial strength and track record let the company pre-qualify for civil projects that smaller, less diversified contractors cannot, which it presents as a barrier to entry for the largest projects.
quotes: Our financial strength, outstanding record of performance on challenging civil works projects, and vertical integration capabilities often enable us to pre-qualify for projects in situations where smaller, less diversified contractors are unable to meet the qualification requirements.

competitive_position.claim: Backlog at the end of Q3 2026 was $20.4 billion. That is up from $19.9 billion at the end of Q2 2026 but down 6% from $21.6 billion a year earlier.
quotes: Consolidated backlog as of September 30, 2026 was $20.4 billion, up compared to $19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026, and down 6% compared to $21.6 billion at the end of the third quarter of 2025.

competitive_position.basis: Figures are from the income statement; the explanation is stated by management in the 10-Q.
competitive_position.claim: Q3 2026 revenue was higher than a year earlier, which the company attributes to newer, larger, higher-margin projects with substantial work remaining.
quotes: The Company experienced strong double-digit growth across all three segments in the third quarter and through the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods last year, primarily driven by increased project execution activities on certain newer, larger and higher-margin projects that have significant scope of work remaining.

competitive_position.basis: Stated by management in the 10-Q and the earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Management says limited competition in select markets for larger projects, together with strong public funding, supports its win rate, and it cites a bid pipeline of more than $200 billion.
quotes: The Company has been successful in winning its share of major new project opportunities over the past several years due to a combination of its strategic bidding approach and favorable market dynamics, including limited competition in select markets for some of the larger projects.

competitive_position.claim: New awards in the first nine months of 2026 were below the prior-year period, though Q3 awards were slightly higher.
quotes: Consolidated new awards for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2.2 billion and $4.5 billion, respectively, compared to $2.0 billion and $7.0 billion for the same periods in 2025.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the balance sheet is consistent with it.
competitive_position.claim: The company reports a net cash position, with cash exceeding total debt as of September 30, 2026.
quotes: the Company's cash exceeded its total debt by $707 million as of September 30, 2026, continuing the Company's strong net cash position.

competitive_position.claim: A July 2026 refinancing extended debt maturities, more than doubled the revolving credit facility and is expected to lower interest expense. It also produced a one-time loss on extinguishment of debt.
quotes: the Company completed the refinancing of its 2024 Senior Notes and entered into an amendment and restatement of its existing revolving credit facility, which, among other things, extended debt maturities, is expected to significantly reduce future interest expense, more than doubled the size of its available revolving credit facility and provided meaningfully improved terms.

competitive_position.claim: Government customers made up 86% of backlog at December 31, 2025, which ties the company's position to public funding and procurement risk.
quotes: The percentage of our business coming from government entities has continued to increase in recent years, and as of December 31, 2025 accounted for 86% of our backlog.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K; whether follow-on funding has passed is not in the evidence.
competitive_position.claim: The current funding window of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law closes on September 30, 2026, and the amount and composition of any follow-on funding is undetermined.
quotes: While the current funding window for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law closes on September 30, 2026, we believe that Congress recognizes the long-term nature of infrastructure work and is already engaged in the legislative process to secure future funding beyond that date, although any amount and composition of such future funding is yet to be determined.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and the earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Contract estimate risk and legal disputes are a named threat: an adverse arbitration decision produced a large non-cash charge that the company is appealing.
quotes: For example, in October 2024, we received an unexpected adverse arbitration decision on a legacy dispute related to a completed Civil segment bridge project in California that resulted in a non-cash charge of $101.6 million, which we are appealing.

competitive_position.claim: Competition for awards is described as intense, and a shift toward progressive design-build delivery could increase competition and lower margins on some future projects.
quotes: In addition, evolving changes in the construction industry, such as the trend toward an increased use of the progressive design-build project delivery method that may reduce project risks for both owners and contractors, could result in increased competition and potentially lower margins on certain projects in the future.

competitive_position.claim: Operations are concentrated in New York and California, which makes the company more exposed to economic conditions in those states.
quotes: Lastly, we are more susceptible to adverse economic conditions in New York and California, as a significant portion of our operations are concentrated in those states.

competitive_position.claim: Rapid backlog growth has constrained skilled labor, and failure to hire and retain personnel is a named threat to executing backlog.
quotes: A significant, rapid growth in our backlog has led, and could continue to lead, to situations in which labor resources become constrained.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the comparison of current assets with current liabilities is read directly from the printed totals.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity is large against short-term obligations. Cash and cash equivalents were 1,111,049 (table in thousands) at the latest balance sheet date, up from 734,553 at year-end. Total current assets of 4,680,655 exceeded total current liabilities of 3,678,699 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: The VIE amounts are stated in the balance sheet line; the availability caveat is inferred and unconfirmed.
financial_health.claim: A large part of reported cash sits in consolidated variable interest entities. 500,168 (table in thousands) of the cash balance is flagged as related to VIEs, against 361,898 at year-end. The evidence does not say how freely this cash can be moved to the parent.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the net cash figure is management's own.
financial_health.claim: Leverage is low in absolute terms and the company holds net cash. Management states total debt of $404 million, down from $407 million at the end of 2025, and cash exceeding total debt by $707 million.
quotes: Total debt as of September 30, 2026 was $404 million, down 1% compared to $407 million at the end of 2025.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet; the link to the refinancing is inferred from the MD&A.
financial_health.claim: Debt on the balance sheet is almost all long-term. Current maturities were 4,563 (table in thousands), down from 14,589. Long-term debt, net of discount and issuance costs, was 399,078 versus 392,785. Unamortized discount and issuance costs fell to 7,444 from 17,983.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the MD&A and cash flow statement; the matching of the proceeds to the refinancing is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Refinancing needs were addressed in the third quarter. The company redeemed its Senior Notes and amended and restated its revolving credit facility. Management says this extended debt maturities, is expected to cut interest expense, and more than doubled the available revolver. The cash flow statement shows proceeds from debt of 400,000 and repayment of debt of 414,272 (table in thousands).
quotes: which, among other things, extended debt maturities, is expected to significantly reduce future interest expense, more than doubled the size of its available revolving credit facility and provided meaningfully improved terms

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement, cash flow statement and MD&A.
financial_health.claim: The refinancing carried a one-time cost. The loss on extinguishment of debt was 51,386 (table in thousands). Management splits it into a $35.6 million cash redemption premium and $15.8 million of non-cash expense. Debt issuance and extinguishment costs paid in cash were 45,880 (table in thousands).
quotes: which consisted of a $35.6 million cash redemption premium and $15.8 million of non-cash expense related to the acceleration of previously unamortized discounts and deferred financing costs

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the income statement; the cause is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Interest expense is lower than a year earlier. For nine months it was 34,407 against 41,489, and for the third quarter 7,290 against 13,549 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement; the drivers are management's explanation.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash generation is strong and rising. Net cash provided by operating activities was 665,063 for nine months against 574,396 a year earlier (table in thousands). Management says the third quarter was $330.9 million, a record, and attributes it to higher volume, execution, earnings and collections on profitable projects.
quotes: The record operating cash flow for both periods was driven by higher volume, strong execution, record earnings and collections on profitable projects.

financial_health.basis: Figures are stated; the quality assessment is inferred from the line items.
financial_health.claim: Part of operating cash flow comes from non-cash add-backs and working capital rather than earnings alone. Net income was 161,475, and the add-backs include share-based compensation of 77,179, a pension settlement charge of 33,753, a loss on extinguishment of 51,386 and deferred income taxes of 57,460. Changes in other working capital components added 249,832 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and balance sheet; the link between the two is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Capital spending is modest relative to operating cash flow. Acquisition of property and equipment was 91,265 against 105,891 a year earlier. Investments in securities were 111,513 against 56,299, and restricted investments rose to 292,316 from 228,959 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement; the prior-year dividend figure is printed as zero.
financial_health.claim: Cash was returned to shareholders and minority partners in addition to debt service. Nine-month payments included dividends of 11,202, stock repurchases of 30,000, and distributions to noncontrolling interests of 23,800. Net cash used in financing was 131,435 (table in thousands). No dividends were paid in the prior-year period.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the risk factor text; the cautionary reading against the refinancing is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Covenant and financing risks were disclosed in the annual report, and the latest 10-Q reports no material changes to risk factors. The 10-K described a substantial amount of indebtedness with restrictive covenants and a net leverage covenant that needed two amendments. Total debt then was $407.4 million, with $14.6 million current.
quotes: We have a substantial amount of indebtedness with restrictive covenants which could adversely affect our financial position and prevent us from fulfilling our obligations under our debt agreements.
There have been no material changes to our risk factors as disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A; revenue figures from the income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Revenue growth is driven by higher execution activity on newer, larger, higher-margin projects. Third-quarter revenue was 1,720,256 against 1,415,360 a year earlier (table in thousands), and the company reports 21.5% growth for the quarter and 17.6% for nine months.
quotes: primarily driven by increased project execution activities on certain newer, larger and higher-margin projects that have significant scope of work remaining

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and 10-Q MD&A; the conversion condition is inferred from them.
growth_thesis.claim: For growth to continue, the large backlog must keep converting to revenue on schedule. Conversion takes several years and differs by segment, and many newer design-build projects are early in a multi-year path.
quotes: Most projects in the Civil segment’s backlog typically convert to revenue over a period of three to five years and in the Building and Specialty Contractors segments over a period of one to three years.

growth_thesis.basis: Backlog and award figures are stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release; the replenishment condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Backlog is the base for future revenue, and it must be replenished. Backlog of $20.4 billion is down 6% from $21.6 billion a year earlier. Nine-month new awards of $4.5 billion compare with $7.0 billion in the prior-year period, so the condition is that new awards keep pace with revenue burn.
quotes: down 6% compared to $21.6 billion at the end of the third quarter of 2025
a second straight quarter with a book-to-burn ratio greater than 1.0x

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management in the earnings release and 10-Q; whether it converts to awards is not shown.
growth_thesis.claim: A large bid pipeline is the source of future awards. The company cites a pipeline of more than $200 billion and expects many large opportunities to bid in the next one to two years, while intending to stay selective on margin and risk.
quotes: Overall, the Company's pipeline of potential projects over the next three to four years totals more than $200 billion, which is approximately three times larger than the pipeline from just a couple of years ago.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the income statement, 10-Q MD&A, earnings release and 10-K MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Profit is growing faster than revenue. Third-quarter income from construction operations was 125,419 versus 40,094 (table in thousands), helped by a $39.5 million decline in share-based compensation. The condition is that execution stays profitable and share-based compensation stays low.
quotes: Share-based compensation expense is expected to decline significantly in 2027, as most of the remaining liability-classified awards will vest by the end of 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Cash flow and balance sheet figures are stated; the reversal risk is inferred from the balance sheet structure.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating cash flow supports growth and capital returns. Nine-month operating cash flow was 665,063 against 574,396 (table in thousands). It funded dividends of 11,202 and repurchases of 30,000, and cash and equivalents reached 1,111,049.
quotes: The record operating cash flow for both periods was driven by higher volume, strong execution, record earnings and collections on profitable projects.

growth_thesis.basis: Debt, cash and interest figures are stated; the future benefit is management's expectation.
growth_thesis.claim: A lower financing cost and net cash position support earnings. Total debt of $404 million is below cash by $707 million, and third-quarter interest expense fell to 7,290 from 13,549 (table in thousands) after the July refinancing. This depends on the refinancing delivering the lower interest cost the company expects.
quotes: is expected to significantly reduce future interest expense

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K; the dependency conclusion is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Demand depends on public infrastructure funding. Government customers were 86% of backlog at the 10-K date, and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding window has closed. Continued growth requires follow-on funding or other state, local and federal sources.
quotes: the current funding window for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law closes on September 30, 2026
as of December 31, 2025 accounted for 86% of our backlog

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management in the earnings release; it is a forward-looking statement, not a result.
growth_thesis.claim: Management expects growth to continue and has raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.90 to $6.10 from $5.15 to $5.45. It also expects continued revenue and adjusted EPS growth in 2027, resting on the long-duration backlog.
quotes: Tutor Perini anticipates continued strong revenue and adjusted EPS growth in 2027 due to clear visibility provided by long-duration backlog
